rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nature study occupies a strategic place because it gathers the sciences and forms the core and greatest achievement of modern physical chemistry.
rows.anchor: علم الطبيعة دائمًا ذو موقع استراتيجي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural philosophy directly precedes modern physical chemistry; understanding its ancient and medieval roots requires studying the host culture’s conception of nature and knowledge.
rows.anchor: فلسفة الطبيعة هي السلف المباشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic intellectual heritage, across its whole and its branches, arose from the cultural upheaval caused by revelation and Islam in tribal society.
rows.anchor: نتيجة لمعلول محدد هو الثورة الثقافية العظمى التي أحدثها نزول الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalam formed the first intellectual circle around revelation before translation-era Greek influence, using reason to understand and establish the text’s implications.
rows.anchor: كأول محاولة لتجاوز النص الديني وإعمال العقل البشري في تفهمه وإثبات مضامينه

rows.speaker: محمد عابد الجابري
rows.claim: Al-Jabiri characterizes kalam as the broadest and most important domain of Arab-Islamic rationality.
rows.anchor: محمد عابد الجابري «العقلانية العربية الإسلامية»

rows.speaker: الشيخ مصطفى عبد الرازق
rows.claim: Mustafa Abd al-Raziq regards kalam as comprehensive Islamic philosophy, including the methodological achievement of legal theory.
rows.anchor: كما رأى الشيخ مصطفى عبد الرازق — الفلسفة الإسلامية الشاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite limitations imposed by its era, kalam’s major positive legacy was shaping distinctly Arab reasoning through philosophical inquiry into questions raised by revelation.
rows.anchor: إيجابية علم الكلام العظمى في أنه تشكل للعقل العربي الصميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalam functioned as a particular Islamic philosophy that prepared the way for general Islamic philosophy, or wisdom.
rows.anchor: الفلسفة الإسلامية الخاصة التي شقت الطريق ومهدته للفلسفة الإسلامية العامة أو الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although kalam and philosophy were relatively distinct paths, their boundary blurred; by the sixth through eighth Islamic centuries their subject matter had converged.
rows.anchor: من القرن السادس الهجري حتى القرن الثامن أصبحت موضوعات علم الكلام هي نفسها موضوعات الفلسفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila especially directed kalam toward philosophy; Ibn Khaldun, despite being Ashʿari, explained the bridge they built.
rows.anchor: المعتزلة لهم دور خاص في توجيه الفكر الكلامي الإسلامي إلى طريق يؤدي في النهاية إلى التفلسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Philosophy developed after kalam matured and differed by starting from concepts rather than immediate social questions and by not taking religious doctrines as premises.
rows.anchor: انطلقت من المفاهيم والمضمون الفكري لا من القضايا المثارة في المجتمع النص بصورة مباشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The study traces conceptions of nature from the theologians through the philosophers to the Arab naturalists conventionally recognized as scientists.
rows.anchor: نتتبع نمو الأصول على أيدي الفلاسفة لنصل إليها مع أولئك الطبائعيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contrary to common assumptions, natural philosophy occupied a broad central place in kalam, even when it was not a conventional headline topic.
rows.anchor: احتلت الطبيعيات في علم الكلام مكانًا فسيحًا في صدر المسرح الفكري

rows.speaker: دي بور
rows.claim: De Boer observes that study of nature predominated among the earliest Muʿtazilites.
rows.anchor: غلب النظر في الطبيعة على المعتزلة الأولين

rows.speaker: الجاحظ
rows.claim: Al-Jahiz held that a true scholar should combine kalam with study of the natural world; he himself regularly described nature’s actions.
rows.anchor: الجاحظ (+ ٢٥٥ﻫ) وهو من رواد النزعة الطبيعية في علم الكلام الاعتزالي

rows.speaker: الجويني
rows.claim: Al-Juwayni defines nature as every existent apart from God, His dominion, and the angels: the physical, observable universe.
rows.anchor: كما قال الجويني إمام الحرمين: «هي كل موجود سوى الله تعالى»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A topical classification of kalam has six areas: divine unity, predestination, faith, threat, imamate, and latāʾif, or natural philosophy.
rows.anchor: تصنيف الموضوعات إلى ستة، هي: التوحيد، القدر، الإيمان، الوعيد، الإمامة ثم اللطائف

rows.speaker: محمد عابد الجابري
rows.claim: Al-Jabiri explains that natural philosophy was called latāʾif, “subtle kalam,” because it involved fine questions assigned to reason rather than scriptural doctrine.
rows.anchor: عابد الجابري — لأنها «دقيق الكلام»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The latāʾif concern body, motion, matter, time, and space: the physical world studied by natural science.
rows.anchor: موضوعها الجسم والحركة والمادة في الزمان والمكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Early theologians’ engagement with latāʾif began Islamic rational inquiry into the physical world and helped science emerge within religious thought.
rows.anchor: بداية اشتباك العقل الإسلامي بالعالم الفيزيقي، وبداية التفكير في الطبيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This religiously embedded beginning helps explain the vigorous scientific movement and the Islamic civilization’s medieval leadership in science.
rows.anchor: زخم الدفع العلمي الذي جعل الحضارة الإسلامية تنفسح للحركة العلمية وتحمل لواءها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic science grew under prevailing ideology and political patronage, unlike modern European science’s conflict with religious authority.
rows.anchor: تتدفق في إطار الأيديولوجيا السائدة وتحت رعاية ومباركة السلطة الحاكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because science remained an effect of Islamic intellectual structures rather than a force reshaping them, its impetus eventually stalled and passed to Europe.
rows.anchor: كان العلم العربي معلولًا ومفعولًا وليس علة فاعلة في تشكيل البنية المعرفية الإسلامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theologians analyzed nature as atoms or substances and accidents, using their succession to argue that the changing world is temporally originated and created by God.
rows.anchor: انحل العالم الطبيعي على أيدي المتكلمين إلى جواهر وأعراض مأخوذة من المذهب الذري القديم

rows.speaker: الجويني
rows.claim: Al-Juwayni treats the created world, in its substances and accidents, as a sign pointing to the existence of the Lord.
rows.anchor: فكذلك «العالَم» بجواهره وأعراضه وأجزائه وأبعاضه دلالة دالة على وجود الرب سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof of origination was broadly accepted: the created world demonstrates God’s existence, power, comprehensive knowledge, wisdom, and life.
rows.anchor: دليل الحدوث، أي كون العالم الحادث المخلوق دليلًا على وجود الله وقدرته وعلمه الشاملين وحكمته وحياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author connects ʿālam (world) with ʿilm and ʿalāma (knowledge and sign), tracing the word’s sensory history through marks and signs.
rows.anchor: كلمة «عالَم» مشتقة أصلًا من العلم والعلامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾan never uses the singular terms ʿālam or ṭabīʿa; it uses al-ʿālamīn seventy-three times and ʿālimīn, from knowledge, three times.
rows.anchor: لم ترد لفظة «العالَم» ولا لفظة الطبيعة في القرآن الكريم أبدًا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalam’s central natural-philosophical problem was the relation of God to the world, framed as creation from nothing and expressed by the proof of origination.
rows.anchor: المشكلة المحورية للطبيعيات الكلامية هي العلاقة بين الله وبين العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof of origination is an empirical analogy from the visible to the unseen, moving from sense perception to intelligible conclusions.
rows.anchor: دليل الحدوث هو في جوهره قياس الغائب على الشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That empirical inference also helped natural inquiry emerge from religious thought, but its closed theological frame later separated kalam from nature research.
rows.anchor: من العوامل التي أدت إلى انفصال علم الكلام عن البحث في الطبيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theological natural philosophy treated nature only as a ladder to establish doctrine, serving theology rather than people living in and needing to understand nature.
rows.anchor: الطبيعيات ليست إلا سلمًا للعقائد، خادمة للإلهيات وليس للإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nature was not pursued as an epistemological problem requiring explanation; only its ontological fact of having begun was needed as evidence for God.
rows.anchor: المطلوب فقط استخدامها كوجود أنطولوجي حدوثه يدلل على وجود الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof of origination kept theology both the starting point and the goal, producing a closed circuit from theology to ontology and back.
rows.anchor: الإلهيات هي النهاية والغاية، مثلما كانت قبلًا هي البداية والمنطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Philosophers made nature more distinct as one of wisdom’s three divisions—rational, natural, and divine—and treated it in dedicated books and sections.
rows.anchor: قسم من أقسام الحكمة الثلاثة: العقليات والطبيعيات والإلهيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theologians, from beginning to end, accepted the world’s origination, although some Muʿtazilites discussed the idea of an eternal creation.
rows.anchor: سلم المتكلمون جميعًا — من أولهم لآخرهم — بأن العالم حادث

rows.speaker: الكندي
rows.claim: Al-Kindi accepted the world’s origination as a question requiring argument, rather than as an unquestioned premise.
rows.anchor: لكن بوصفها محل نظر ومحتاجة لبرهان «الكندي»

rows.speaker: الفارابي وابن سينا
rows.claim: Under Greek influence, al-Farabi and Ibn Sina used emanation as an alternative framework for explaining the world’s origin.
rows.anchor: والصدور كبديل «الفارابي وابن سينا»

rows.speaker: ابن رشد
rows.claim: Ibn Rushd rejects emanation and argues that the world is eternal yet created, representing a later synthesis in the debate.
rows.anchor: ثم رفض ابن رشد هذا البديل وأسرف في تبيان أن العالم قديم ومخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite their disputes, philosophers kept nature within ontology oriented toward God, so their natural philosophy did not fundamentally escape kalam’s theological direction.
rows.anchor: ظلت الطبيعة قابعة دائمًا في قلب الأنطولوجيا المتجهة أولًا وأخيرًا نحو المتجه الإلهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The naturalists deserve recognition as direct bearers of Arab scientific heritage and inclusion in philosophy, which then encompassed significant rational inquiry.
rows.anchor: الذين يتحملون المسئولية المباشرة للتراث العلمي العربي، المعروفون باسم الطبائعيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theologians called naturalists heretics; although their philosophy was often unsystematic and empirically focused, philosophical questions shaped their contribution to science and philosophy.
rows.anchor: المتكلمين عدوهم زنادقة ملحدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the second Islamic century, Jabir ibn Hayyan viewed nature and all its contents as alive, rational, and willing; celestial bodies were living powers affecting the world.
rows.anchor: إيمانه الطاغي بحيوية الطبيعة وكل شيء فيها، بل رآها عاقلة مريدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Jabir, celestial bodies differed from God through their material component; his strong vitalism and astrology may explain their persistence in Islamic natural thought.
rows.anchor: الفرق بينها وبين الله هو دخول المادة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links the enduring vitalist and astrological currents partly to early naturalists and to Hermetic and Gnostic elements transmitted by ancient sciences.
rows.anchor: فلا ننسى دور علوم الأوائل وما حملته من تيارات غنوصية وهرمسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the fourth century, al-Razi shared an enthusiastic belief in nature’s vitality and astrology; theologians branded him a major atheist outside Islam.
rows.anchor: آمن بحيوية الطبيعة والتنجيم الطبيب العالم أبو بكر الرازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi fully adopted the Harranian position; the Harranians were associated with anthropomorphism and Sabianism and stressed celestial bodies’ power over nature and human life.
rows.anchor: تبنى موقف الحرانيين تبنِّيًا كاملًا

rows.speaker: محمد عابد الجابري
rows.claim: Al-Jabiri attributes Hermetic and Gnostic elements in Eastern philosophy to a transition from bayan toward irfan.
rows.anchor: أدت إلى انتقال البيان إلى العرفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejected miracles and prophecy, holding that all people can contact the upper world through purification of the soul and detachment from the senses.
rows.anchor: أنكر مثلهم المعجزات والنبوة لأن الناس سواسية في إمكان الاتصال بالعالم العلوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi posited five eternal principles—matter, form or soul, time, place, and motion—making creation from nothing impossible; creation arose from the soul’s longing for matter.
rows.anchor: بقدمائهم الخمسة: الهيولي، والصورة أو النفس، والزمان، والمكان، والحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi mocked idealist emanation, but advances in natural science let him redirect emanation in a more materialist direction.
rows.anchor: مكَّنه من توجيه نظرية الفيض توجيهًا ماديًّا أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naturalists generally left Pythagoreanism and emanation behind and followed Aristotelian thought loosely, focusing on material phenomena and their effects.
rows.anchor: وساروا مع الأرسطية عمومًا وبصفة غير ملزمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite empirical interests, naturalists ultimately moved beyond nature, reason, and soul to God as first cause or wise maker, whose wisdom and beneficence appear in creation.
rows.anchor: جاوزوا الطبيعة والعقل والنفس في أبحاثهم، وارتقوا إلى ذات الله فجعلوه العلة الأولى

rows.speaker: البيروني
rows.claim: Al-Biruni illustrates the theological trajectory by saying geometric training proceeds from natural signs to divine signs.
rows.anchor: ثم ترتقي بواسطة التدريب بها من المعالم الطبيعية إلى المعالم الإلهية

rows.speaker: ابن الهيثم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Haytham rejects the theologians’ proof of the world’s origination as flawed and holds that an eternal world undergoes continuous creation, as Ibn Rushd did.
rows.anchor: يرفض طريق المتكلمين، ويبرهن على أن دليل حدوث العالم عندهم فاسد

rows.speaker: ابن الهيثم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Haytham wrote a treatise exposing the error of those who claimed that God was eternally inactive and then began to act.
rows.anchor: مقالة في إبانة غلط من قضى أن الله لم يزل غير فاعل ثم فعل

rows.speaker: ابن الهيثم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Haytham divides knowledge into mathematics, natural science, and divine science.
rows.anchor: ينقسم العلم معه انقسامًا ثلاثيًّا إلى رياضي وطبيعي وإلهي

rows.speaker: ابن الهيثم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Haytham says geometry and logic lead through natural principles and causes to divine knowledge and recognition of God’s wisdom, power, and knowledge.
rows.anchor: فإن به وبالمنطلق يوصل إلى علم الأمور الطبيعية، التي هي الحكمة

rows.speaker: برتراند رسل
rows.claim: Russell observes that medieval Arab scientists pursued particular facts rather than universal laws or scientific systems, making them excessively empirical.
rows.anchor: اتصلت بالوقائع الجزئية دون القوانين الكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nature remained oriented toward divinity and ontology rather than human epistemology; this explains the lack of historical continuity and systematic scientific theories.
rows.anchor: بعيدة عن نظرية المعرفة التي هي مجال التنامي والصيرورة والفعالية الإنسانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although naturalists did not formulate scientific systems, their serious empirical work on particular laws provided necessary precursors to modern science.
rows.anchor: كانت هذه الجهود مقدمات ضرورية لنسق العلم الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says modern knowledge must sever the theological direction, while historically it shaped Islamic natural philosophy, which resisted full commitment to materialist or idealist Greek schools.
rows.anchor: فإنه صنع الملامح الخاصة للطبيعيات الإسلامية في ذلك العصر الوسيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islamic thought could deny nature’s independence but not its objective existence, since the natural world is a concrete effect of divine power.
rows.anchor: أما وجوده الموضوعي فلا؛ لأن العالم الطبيعي فعلًا متعينًا للقدرة الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic thinkers extensively appropriated Greek traditions while interpreting them through their own cultural constants.
rows.anchor: أسرفوا في استغلال وتسخير التراث اليوناني، لكن كل هذا في إطار تصوراتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author presents Arabic-Islamic thought as an independent synthesis of materialism and idealism, a developmental step that remained within its era’s idealist theological frame.
rows.anchor: تيارًا مستقلًّا في النظر إلى العالم الطبيعي، استوعب ذينك الطرفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The survey aims to show both the strengths that produced a rich Arab scientific heritage and the internal and external weaknesses that contributed to its decline.
rows.anchor: مواطن القوة التي خلقت التراث العلمي العربي الزاخر، مثلما أبان عن مواطن الضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invocation praises God for creating the human being in the best form after a drop of semen, then honoring the human being and preparing him to receive revelation.
rows.anchor: وخلقه في أحسن تقويم بعد كون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author invokes the Qurʾan’s exalted standing in the heavenly register as part of his praise of the divine gift of scripture.
rows.anchor: وقد قال سبحانه فيه: (وإنه في أم الكتاب لدينا لعلي حكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is praised as the chosen prophet endowed with the Book and clear proofs that open the path for people of insight.
rows.anchor: المخصوص بالكتاب، والفاتح لأولي البصائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited warning says that only one who follows the Reminder and fears the Merciful unseen benefits from the Messenger’s warning.
rows.anchor: إنما تنذر من اتبع الذكر وخشي الرحمن بالغيب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says every prophet received signs sufficient for people to believe, while his own special gift was revelation, through which he hopes to have the most followers on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: اعتبرت قوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: " ما من نبي إلا وقد أعطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the Prophet had countless miracles besides the Qurʾan, but the Qurʾan is the clearest, wisest, most guiding, and most enduring miracle.
rows.anchor: بدروب لا يحصيها العد، ولا كاد تنحصر بالحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾan joins proof and testimony with clarification of the path and the condition of each group, and remains directly observable to those who reflect.
rows.anchor: فإنما ضمنت إلى - الدلالة والشهادة إيضاح الطربق وأعلمت بحال كل فريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike other miracles known through later reports rather than direct observation, the Qurʾan remains pure and present for reflection across the ages.
rows.anchor: وليس كالعيان، فلله ما أعظمها معجزة باقية مدى الدهور

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: In a report cited from Sahih Muslim, Hudhayfa recounts praying at night with the Prophet, who recited al-Baqara, then al-Nisaʾ, then Aal ʿImran; Hudhayfa repeatedly wondered when he would bow.
rows.anchor: روينا في صحيح مسلم عن حذيفة رضى الله عنه قال
